markdown:
# Product foundation

## Product
Chaser sends polite payment reminders for freelance designers so they stop chasing late invoices by hand. Chaser is a working name, not fixed.

## Problem
Freelance designers hate asking for money. Today they keep a spreadsheet and write awkward emails weeks after the due date, or let it slide. They lose a few hours a month on it.

## Persona
A freelance brand or web designer working alone, with 3 to 10 active clients. They invoice from a tool like Wave or from a PDF. They want the money without asking for it. Hating the ask stops them.

## Core scenario
On a Monday morning at their desk, on a laptop, a designer sees an invoice two weeks overdue. They want to hand it to Chaser in under a minute and not think about it again until the money lands. It happens a few times a month.

## Also affected
The designer's clients, who get the reminders. They should feel nudged, not accused.

## Not for
Agencies with a finance person.

## Feel
Calm, friendly, a bit dry.
Never pushy, corporate or cute.

## Goals
1. 50 paying users by the end of March 2027.

Earns by: See Open.

## Anti-goals
1. We will not build invoicing itself.
2. No mobile app.

## Assumptions
Designers will let a tool email their clients in their name.

## Open
- Goals: "Grow fast after that" has no number and no date.
- Goals: "Paying users" has no price or plan.
- Goals: Earns by is empty. Nothing says how Chaser makes money.
- Anti-goals: Neither anti-goal says why.
- Core scenario: How an invoice reaches Chaser (Wave, PDF, other) is not said.
- Assumptions: Nothing says how or when we will test the one assumption.

questions.question: How does Chaser charge the designer: flat fee, per invoice, or a share of money recovered?
questions.why: Earns by is empty, and the way it earns decides what counts as a paying user and whether the goal fits a designer with only a few late invoices a month.

questions.question: What price per month would a paying user pay, so we can turn 50 users into revenue?
questions.why: Without a price, 50 paying users could mean 50 dollars or 5,000 dollars a month, and nobody can say whether the goal is worth it.

questions.question: What comes after March 2027: a second goal with a number and date, or none for now?
questions.why: The note about growing fast afterward has no number or date, so it can't be checked and belongs in Goals only if it gets both.

questions.question: What evidence do you have that designers lose real money or hours to late invoices, beyond your own sense of it?
questions.why: The Problem rests on a claim of a few hours a month with no source, and a small loss may not justify paying for a tool.

questions.question: Wave and similar invoicing tools already send automatic reminders, so why would a designer who uses one switch to Chaser?
questions.why: The persona invoices from Wave or a PDF, so the main alternative is a built-in feature at no extra cost, and the document names no reason to leave it.

questions.question: How and when will you test that designers will let a tool email their clients in their name?
questions.why: If this is false the product has no use, yet the document names no test, date or pass mark.

questions.question: Should Chaser ever escalate when a client stays silent, with a firmer tone, late fees or a collections referral?
questions.why: Escalation is the obvious next feature for a reminder tool, and it would break the Feel (never pushy) and the promise that clients feel nudged, not accused.
options: Only if the designer opts in

questions.question: Will Chaser ever take the payment itself, such as a pay button or payment link inside a reminder?
questions.why: Collecting money is a tempting step beyond reminding, and it brings regulation and blurs the invoicing anti-goal, so the document needs a clear line.

questions.question: Why do we refuse to build invoicing, and does that rule out importing or syncing invoices from Wave?
questions.why: Without a reason, a team cannot tell if a Wave import or a payment-details page counts as invoicing, and the open item on how invoices reach Chaser depends on it.
options: Wave and PDFs stay the source
Too big for a small team

questions.question: In that under-a-minute Monday moment, how does the overdue invoice get to Chaser?
questions.why: Wave, PDF and a forwarded email are three different products, and the persona names both Wave and PDF, so two readers would picture different moments.
options: Both Wave and PDF at launch

questions.question: Should Chaser turn away other freelancers (developers, writers) and two or three person studios, or take them?
questions.why: Not for names only agencies with a finance person, yet Persona says designers working alone, so a freelance writer or small studio could sign up and the document does not say if they are welcome.

questions.question: Do the reminder emails sound like Chaser, or like the designer who sends them?
questions.why: Feel must suit the clients who read the emails as well as the designer who uses the app, and a dry Chaser voice sent in the designer's name could clash with how they write.
